record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For user-level central differential privacy in cross-device federated learning, how can algorithms adaptively bound heterogeneous user contributions, clip model updates, characterize privacy-accuracy trade-offs when user contribution counts vary widely, and determine whether privacy-amplification-by-iteration results extend to non-convex learning?

evidence.quote: user-level DP is fundamentally less understood

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cross-device federated learning setting in which a central server iteratively trains a model by repeatedly sampling a subset of users from a large population, requesting each sampled user to compute a model update from its local data, and aggregating these updates. Let the parameter space be $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $f(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{u \sim \mathcal{U}}[f_u(\theta)]$ denote the global objective, where $\mathcal{U}$ is the distribution over users and $f_u$ is user $u$'s local (possibly non-convex) loss, and assume each user $u$ holds a variable, heterogeneous number $n_u$ of records.

A randomized training mechanism $M$ satisfies user-level $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-central differential privacy if for any two populations $D, D'$ that differ in the entire data of one user, and every measurable event $S$ in the output space, $\Pr[M(D)\in S] \le e^{\varepsilon}\Pr[M(D')\in S] + \delta$. In each round $t$, user $u$ returns an update $\Delta_u^{(t)}$ which is clipped to norm at most $C_u^{(t)}$ and aggregated with Gaussian noise of scale $\sigma$ added to enforce the user-level DP guarantee.

Address the following:

(1) Design an algorithm that, without prior knowledge of individual user contribution magnitudes $\|\Delta_u^{(t)}\|$ or counts $n_u$, adaptively selects per-user clipping thresholds $C_u^{(t)}$ in a way that is itself user-level differentially private and that bounds the influence of any single user on the aggregated update.

(2) Provide a tight analysis of the privacy–utility trade-off (utility measured by convergence rate or excess empirical risk of $f$) for the resulting mechanism in the regime where the distribution of $n_u$ across users is highly heavy-tailed.

(3) Determine whether the privacy-amplification-by-iteration phenomenon — by which only the final iterate of a contractive noisy iterative process is released and the effective privacy loss decays with the number of intermediate hidden steps — can be extended from convex losses to (smooth) non-convex losses $f_u$ in the federated user-level setting, by either proving such an amplification result with explicit dependence on smoothness, step size, noise scale, and number of iterations, or proving that no such non-trivial amplification is possible in general.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2023–2025) on user-level DP in federated learning (e.g., Uldp-FL, adaptive clipping schemes, DP-SCAFFOLD) provide partial results on adaptive per-user clipping and convergence under non-convex objectives, but a unified, tight analysis for heavy-tailed heterogeneous user contributions and a general privacy-amplification-by-iteration result for non-convex losses remain unresolved. The problem is broadly considered open in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Uldp-FL: Federated Learning with Across-Silo User-Level Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: User-level DP guaranteed via per-user weighted clipping in cross-silo FL.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on user-level DP with adaptive clipping, but not the full open problem.

status_evidence.title: Federated Learning with Formal Differential Privacy Guarantees (Google)
status_evidence.snippet: Production deployment uses user-level DP with adaptive clipping; trade-offs depend strongly on user contribution heterogeneity.
status_evidence.claim: User-level DP analyses remain heuristic for heavy-tailed user contributions.

status_evidence.title: Privacy Amplification for Federated Learning via User Sampling and Wireless Aggregation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies amplification via sampling; does not resolve amplification-by-iteration for non-convex losses.
status_evidence.claim: Amplification-by-iteration in non-convex FL settings is unresolved.
